thesis: TMX Group Limited (X.TO) operates Canada's primary market infrastructure: Toronto Stock Exchange and TSX Venture Exchange for equity capital formation, Montréal Exchange and BOX for derivatives, CDS for clearing and settlement, Alpha for alternative trading, and global data and analytics businesses including TMX Trayport (energy trading connectivity) and TMX VettaFi (ETF indexing). **[Fact]** The group reported **$1,717.2 million** of revenue in FY2025 and **$488.2 million** in Q1/26 (`X.TO/investor-documents/ir-tmx/annual_report_2025.pdf`, `X.TO/investor-documents/ir-tmx/q1_2026_mda.pdf`). Revenue is overwhelmingly fee-based on listings, trading volumes, clearing, and recurring data subscriptions rather than balance-sheet lending.
why_market_wrong: The market may treat TMX as a slow Canadian listings utility while underpricing the shift toward recurring global data and analytics. **[Inference]** Global Insights (GSIA) reached **$701.8 million** in FY2025 revenue (+16% year-over-year), now **41%** of consolidated revenue, with TMX Trayport and VettaFi driving double-digit growth. **[Inference]** At **~$50** per share (CAD), the stock trades near **~22 times** mid-cycle owner cash, which prices in quality but leaves limited margin of safety versus our **~15%** annual return target. There is **no dated predictive attribute** in our base case; the inefficiency is descriptive (quality compounder at full price), not a timed catalyst.
